meta: Jean-Léon Gérôme's 1864 painting of Siamese ambassadors received by Napoleon III at Fontainebleau, ordered for the Versailles galleries.
about: A formal audience fills a gilded hall, with officers and court ladies gathered around an imperial throne beneath red drapery. The state commissioned the picture in 1861 for the historical galleries at Versailles. Gérôme began it in his studio on the rue de Bruxelles in Paris and finished it in 1864. It was shown at the next Salon. The state paid 20,000 francs for it, and Napoleon III kept it in his collection. In 2017 it was deposited at the château of Fontainebleau.

meta: Jan Steen's small panel Girl Eating Oysters, about 1658: a young woman in a red jacket opens an oyster at a laid table.
about: A young woman in a red jacket trimmed with white fur sits at a table and opens an oyster while looking straight at the viewer. More oysters lie nearby with a bread roll, a knife, a wine glass and a jug. Jan Steen painted the small panel about 1658. Wikipedia says he used oysters as a symbol of earthly lust. It has been in the Mauritshuis in The Hague since 1936.

meta: Rembrandt's 1632 group portrait of Dr Nicolaes Tulp explaining the arm muscles of a corpse to Amsterdam surgeons.
about: Nicolaes Tulp holds forceps to the exposed forearm muscles of a corpse and explains them to men in black clothes and white ruffs. Rembrandt painted it in 1632 for the Surgeons Guild to hang in their meeting room. Some of the doctors paid to be included. The signature at upper left may be the first time he used his first name instead of a monogram. In 1828 the guild's widow fund planned to sell it, but King William I blocked that by decree. The Dutch state bought it instead and placed it in the Mauritshuis.

meta: Gustav Klimt's The Kiss, painted in 1907 and 1908 and first exhibited as Liebespaar, now in the Belvedere in Vienna.
about: A couple embrace inside a golden robe patterned with rectangles and circles. The man bends over the woman's face, and she rests a hand against his cheek. Klimt painted it in 1907 and 1908. It was exhibited in 1908 under the title Liebespaar, meaning the lovers. Wikipedia places it in his Golden Period and says the oil is combined with gold leaf, silver and platinum. The robes show the influence of Art Nouveau. It hangs in the Belvedere in Vienna.

meta: Jacopo de' Barbari's Portrait of Luca Pacioli, around 1500: a friar draws geometry beside an unidentified young man, in Naples.
about: A friar holds a stylus over a geometric diagram on a wooden tablet while a young man in a fur-trimmed coat stands beside him. A glass polyhedron hangs at the left. Wikipedia names the friar as the mathematician Luca Pacioli and attributes the painting to Jacopo de' Barbari, around 1500. It adds that Leonardo da Vinci, a collaborator of Pacioli, may have painted part of it. The young man is not firmly identified, but Wikipedia says he could be Albrecht Dürer. The painting is in the Capodimonte Museum in Naples.

meta: Edwin Long's 1875 painting of a Babylonian marriage auction, now at Royal Holloway, University of London.
about: A crowded interior centres on a raised platform where a veiled woman stands. Edwin Long took the scene from Herodotus, who described young women in Babylon being auctioned into marriage. Wikipedia says the painting drew attention for its provocative treatment of women and that Long's historical detail was well regarded. Thomas Holloway bought it in 1882. Royal Holloway, University of London, owns it now.

meta: Paolo Veronese's Cephalus and Procris, about 1584: the moment Procris dies as her husband tries to understand her.
about: Procris dies while her bewildered husband Cephalus tries to understand her and to explain himself. Paolo Veronese took the tragic couple from Ovid's Metamorphoses and made the picture as a pendant to his Venus and Adonis, now in the Prado. Diego Velázquez bought it in Venice in 1641 for the Spanish royal collection. Joseph Bonaparte took it out of that collection during his brief rule of Spain. After several sales, Wilhelm von Bode bought it for the Strasbourg museum in 1912.

meta: A gouache after Lam Qua of a woman with a large tumour on her right hand, linked to a case in Peter Parker's records.
about: A woman reclines in a blue robe and hides her face with one hand while a large tumour swells on her right hand. The Wellcome record says Rachman identified her with case 5721 in Peter Parker's report. According to the quoted passage, the patient was told she could go home whenever she liked, but she preferred to stay longer where everything was provided. Her husband came back for her and she was discharged on 19 January, both of them thankful. The gouache was made after Lam Qua around 1838.

meta: A gouache after Lam Qua of Po Ashing, a man with a large tumour on his left arm, matched to Peter Parker's case 2152.
about: A seated man in a black cap holds a small white object while a large pink tumour hangs from his left arm. He sits on a wooden stool before a plain pale background. The Wellcome record ties the gouache to case 2152 in Peter Parker's report, dated 3 November 1836. It notes that the tumour was treated by amputation at the shoulder joint. The operation took less than one minute. The gouache was made after Lam Qua.

meta: Jacques-Joseph Lecurieux's lithograph of Salomon de Caus in the Bicêtre asylum, a scene from an invented story.
about: A bearded prisoner behind a barred window holds out a paper to a man in a feathered hat and a woman in a white gown, while ragged figures crowd the courtyard. The scene belongs to a story in which Salomon de Caus tried to persuade Louis XIII that he had invented a steam carriage and Richelieu had him locked up in the Bicêtre asylum. A Wellcome note citing Fiske and Delepierre says Henri Berthoud invented the tale in 1834 to go with a Gavarni drawing of a madman at the bars of his cell.

meta: The three Marys at the tomb, a panel from the Eyck circle, dated 1410 to 1426 and now in Rotterdam.
about: Three women in coloured robes approach a stone tomb where an angel sits on the open lid, while armed soldiers sleep on the ground. Wikipedia names the women as Mary Jacobi, Mary Magdalene and Mary Salome. The panel is usually given to Hubert van Eyck, Jan's older brother, but the attribution is disputed. Erwin Panofsky saw a collaboration of both men, and others see Jan's workshop or Jan alone. Estimates of the date run from 1410 to 1426.
